title: Trust over control: how Cris Pop leads Thunder by letting an intern grow beyond her role
summary: Cris Pop frames his leadership philosophy through an intern story: when Sabina asked to write outside her role, he said yes and the result surfaced a voice that rigid job descriptions would have buried. The essay argues that trust, psychological safety and betting on potential produce stronger people than micromanagement.

principles.text: Leadership means breaking the walls around people, not drawing boxes; nurture raw potential even when it leads somewhere unplanned.
principles.quote: My work as a leader is not about drawing boxes around people. It’s about breaking the walls that confine them.

principles.text: Say yes when someone asks to step outside their role; a request like that is a spark, not a deviation.
principles.quote: I didn’t see it as stepping out of role but a spark beginning to be ignited.

principles.text: Managing by job descriptions and lanes buries valuable voices; listening surfaces what people carry.
principles.quote: If I'd been focused on job descriptions and staying in lanes, if I'd been managing instead of listening, this voice would have stayed buried.

principles.text: Expectations of people are usually too small; give space and bet on potential instead of policing boundaries.
principles.quote: when you bet on potential instead of policing boundaries, you get transformation.

principles.text: Trusted people rise and create things micromanagement can never manufacture.
principles.quote: when people feel trusted, they rise. They don’t just deliver, they soar. They create things no amount of micromanagement could ever manufacture.

principles.text: People grow in freedom, and trust accelerates growth; micromanagement yields workers, trust yields giants.
principles.quote: That people grow in freedom. That trust is the ultimate accelerant.
